ratings.reviewer_notes: Direct model evidence only: Ciliatoside A inhibited NLRP3 activation in BV-2 cells and improved pathology in 3xTg-AD mice; no human AD evidence is reported.
Direct mouse evidence that HSV-1 activates the NLRP3 pathway and that inflammasome blockade reduces amyloid deposition and cognitive decline in infected 5xFAD mice.
Review concerns microglial neuroinflammation in cardiovascular diseases and does not address NLRP3 activation in AD.
Direct human postmortem evidence, importantly negative: temporal cortex from AD cases showed astrocyte activation but no significant differences in measured NLRP3 activation markers versus controls.
Reports lower BHB in human AD blood cells and brain, but the mechanistic evidence that BHB inhibits NLRP3 and reduces AD pathology comes from 5XFAD mice.
Direct AD mouse and cultured-microglia evidence that glutamine metabolism promotes NLRP3 activation and that glutaminase suppression limits activation through AMPK/mTORC1-regulated mitophagy.

Combines APP/PS1 experiments showing amyloid-associated NLRP3 assembly and amplified IL-1β responses with human AD brain findings of elevated IL-1β and IL-6 during infection; the causal NLRP3 work is primarily murine.
Direct mouse evidence that systemic LPS impairs microglial amyloid clearance and that NLRP3 knockout blocks microglial and amyloid-pathology changes in APP/PS1 mice.
Review-level synthesis of NLRP3 mechanisms and APP/PS1 knockout findings; useful for distinguishing mechanistic mouse claims but provides no primary human evidence.
Review of microglial NLRP3 activation in AD, including protection from memory loss and amyloid deposition in transgenic mice; not a primary human-versus-mouse study.

Direct mixed-species evidence: human AD retina shows elevated NLRP3 and activation products, while neuronal cultures and APP/PS1 mice test infection-induced inflammasome activation and disease worsening.

Human postmortem study localizing NLRP3 mainly to microglia and finding ASC/caspase-1-associated changes across early and intermediate AD pathology. It supports inflammasome protein expression, though functional NLRP3 activation is less directly established.
Direct mouse and microglial model evidence that GPCR19 ligation suppresses P2X7R-mediated NLRP3 activation and improves amyloid, neuroinflammation, neuronal loss, and memory in 5xFAD mice.
Direct 5XFAD knockout and BV-2 evidence that p62-dependent autophagic degradation of NLRP3 reduces microglial inflammation/pyroptosis and preserves amyloid phagocytosis; no human evidence.
Direct APP/PS1 mouse and BV-2 evidence that semaglutide suppresses microglial NLRP3 signaling, with NLRP3 knockdown corroborating effects on amyloid, inflammation, polarization, and ferroptosis.

Direct APP/PS1 evidence that amyloid triggers NLRP3 and that NLRP3 loss or chronic inhibition alters glutaminolysis and enhances microglial amyloid clearance. Conservation was tested in human cells, not human AD tissue.

Direct 5xFAD and cultured-human-microglia evidence that hiPSC neural-stem-cell vesicles reduce NLRP3-associated signaling and inflammasome products; it does not provide evidence from human AD patients.

Direct human peripheral-monocyte evidence: assembled NLRP3 complexes, component colocalization, and IL-1β/IL-18 production increased in AD, whereas MCI showed increased NLRP3 without functional assembly.

Direct experimental-model evidence that tau activates NLRP3 and that loss of inflammasome function reduces tau phosphorylation and aggregation; supports a causal mouse-model link from amyloid-driven microglial activation to tau pathology.

Key human-versus-mouse comparison: human MCI and AD brains showed enhanced active caspase-1, while causal protection from memory loss, inflammation, and amyloid deposition was demonstrated using Nlrp3- or Casp1-deficient APP/PS1 mice.

Adjacent mouse evidence: nicotinamide riboside reduced NLRP3 expression in APP/PS1 brains, but the mechanistic focus is NAD+ depletion and cGAS-STING rather than direct testing of NLRP3 activation. Human evidence is limited to AD fibroblast cytoplasmic DNA.
